newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL assigns "P1+" rating to Saw Pipes.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL assigns "P1+" rating to Saw Pipes.

text.p: The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Wednesday it had assigned a "P1+" rating to the commercial paper programme of Saw Pipes Limited (SPL) indicating that the degree of safety regarding timely payment on the instrument is very strong.
An "FAA" rating has been assigned to SPL's fixed deposit programme indicating that the degree of safety regarding timely payment of interest and principal is strong, CRISIL said.

SPL was promoted by the O.P. Jindal group in 1984, primarily for the manufacture of submerged arc welded (SAW) U-O-E pipes which are used for high pressure critical applications in the oil and gas sector. It is the country's sole domestic player.

However, since 1994/95, the company has commissioned a seamless tube plant of capacity of 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes per annum capacity and a 100,000 tonne-per-annum spiral pipe plant at Nasik, Maharashtra.

CRISIL said SPL has entered and sucessfully established itself in the capital intensive SAW pipeline business by setting-up manufacturing facilities based on secondhand plant and machinery and by securing the necessary accreditations and approvals which are likely to serve as strong entry barriers.
Competition from international players is countered largely by freight disadvantage and low labour and capital costs.

The short- to medium-term outlook for the pipeline industry appears to be favourable mainly on account of a number of major projects proposed by public sector oil companies in the domestic market and expected initiation of new onshore and offshore projects worldwide.

However, CRISIL said, this business is order-driven and capacity utilisation has to be ensured all the times. The cyclical nature of the business may influence sales turnover and profits accordingly though operating cash flows from this division have been fairly strong in the past.
In addition, the company's seam less tubes business has also failed to stabilise and is currently making losses.
